Issued at 203 PM CDT Tue Sep 22 2026

Drizzle and sprinkles are expected to end this afternoon as a 
weak ridge continues to build in over the northern Plains. 
Soundings indicate some thinning of the stratus deck in the mid 
afternoon, which may allow a few peaks of sunshine. But for the 
most part cloudy conditions will prevail through the weekend. 
Winds this afternoon will be slightly breezy out of the east-
southeast, with gusts of 15 mph up to 20 mph over central South 
Dakota. Highs will be 10-15 degrees cooler than average for this
time of year, in the upper 50s to low 60s. (Average is mid 
70s.)

Looking aloft and to the west, we see an upper trough lifting 
northeast out of the central Rockies through the day. As it 
ejects out onto the northern Plains this afternoon a lee trough 
will form from Montana down to Colorado. As this wave system 
pushes slowly east the SPG will tighten, strengthening the LLJ.
Winds from the surface through 850 mb will be south- 
southeasterly, advecting in warmer and moist air. CAMs have 
begun to key on some light showers developing along a band of 
vorticity advection over central South Dakota in the late 
afternoon today. These will be light and scattered in nature, 
driven by both the increasing WAA and LLJ. These will slowly 
advect east through the overnight and into the day Wednesday. 
Meanwhile, breezy winds will expand slowly east through the 
overnight and much of the day Wednesday. Gusts of 20-30 mph are 
expected along and west of I-29, with gusts up to 40 mph 
possible over central South Dakota Wednesday afternoon. Areas 
east of I-29 will see lighter gusts between 15-20 mph. Highs for
Wednesday will be slightly warmer thanks to the enhanced WAA, 
in the 60s. 

By Wednesday afternoon the previously mentioned wave system will be 
drifting over central North and South Dakota. Increasing 
positive vorticity advection from both the northern wave and a 
secondary band moving in from the southwest ahead of a 
subtropical wave will result in stronger forcing for ascent. 
Coupled with continued WAA and strong LLJ a more organized line 
of storms will form with the potential for pockets of moderate 
to heavy rain. We do not anticipate severe weather at this time,
however localized ponding is possible. Storms are expected to 
form over central South Dakota by Wednesday afternoon and slowly
move east through the evening and overnight. By sunrise 
Thursday storms should be approaching the I-29 corridor and 
continue east through the remainder of the morning. 

Thursday late afternoon to early evening showers let up briefly as 
the LLJ and WAA decrease. The previously mentioned subtropical wave 
begins to accelerate northeast out of the southern Rockies through 
the overnight hours of Thursday into Friday. The LLJ and WAA once 
again increase with the wave's approach and showers and 
thunderstorms reintensify along and south of Highway 20. These 
will push slowly north-northeast with the wave through Friday 
evening. Hot on the heels of the first wave, a second shortwave 
will push through overnight Friday into Saturday. This round 
also has the potential for brief periods of heavy rainfall. 
These will gradually push east and rain will cease from west to 
east through Saturday afternoon before exiting east of the CWA 
Saturday night. 

In total from 7pm tonight until 7pm Saturday ensemble guidance 
indicates a high probability (> 80%) of widespread 0.25 inches of 
rain. A narrow corridor from Yankton northeast to Marshall, MN also 
has a high probability (> 80%) of seeing 0.50 inches. With a small 
bullseye from Yankton to Sioux Falls with about a 75% probability of 
an inch or more. We finally get a break from all the rain on Sunday, 
with hopes for sunshine Sunday afternoon. Highs during the remainder 
of the week will be in the 60s to low 70s thanks to the southerly 
winds and strong WAA in the mid-levels. Sunday, however, the sun 
should warm us nicely into the low to mid 70s. Unfortunately our 
break is short, as an active pattern returns Monday through the 
first half of next week.
